UniverSat

Resolution- and modality-agnostic transformers for Earth observation

Yohann Perron* · Guillaume Astruc* · Nicolas Gonthier · Clément Mallet · Loïc Landrieu

*equal contribution · LASTIG, Univ Gustave Eiffel, IGN, ENSG · CNES · LIGM, ENPC, IPP · EFEO

Problem

Earth observation data comes in every shape

aerial optical satellite radar hyperspectral elevation
10 cm → 250 mper pixel
1 → 396spectral channels
1 → 150dates per sample

A ViT expects one shape

Fixed patch size, channels and dates. The usual fixes: resample, drop channels, or train one encoder per sensor.

UniverSat covers the whole space

One set of weights, trained jointly on 13 sensors from 7 datasets, at native resolution.

Training set as diverse as possible

Even a new sensor should fall in the convex hull of seen sensors.

Method · Universal Patch Encoder

One encoder turns a patch of any shape into a token

01

New paradigm: a patch is a set of atoms

ViTs project a fixed C × P × P patch with a sensor-specific layer. We go down to the atom: one pixel × one band × one date.

Each atom is embedded from its value + metadata: the encoder knows what it measures, not just where it sits.

02

Dimension aggregation

We sequentially collapse each dimension with Axial Cross-Attention. As we collapse dimensions, we increase the feature size.

03

Final output

A high-dimensional vector representing the observation

One token per patch, whatever the sensor, passed to the transformer.

Method · Architecture

Any sensors in, any output resolution out

Each sensor arrives at its native resolution, bands and dates. Nothing is resampled.

Patches are defined in metres, so the same UPE puts every sensor on one token grid.

Axial cross-attention merges the sensors, then a standard transformer reasons over space.

The latent grid is resampled to any resolution and cross-attends to sub-patch tokens.

Training

Self-supervised on 13 sensors at once

0%of atoms dropped: whole sensors, bands, dates and patches

Results · generalization

It reads a hyperspectral sensor it never saw in training

EnMAP · hyperspectral · 30 m

SpectralEarth benchmark, 7 tasks. UniverSat never saw EnMAP during pretraining; DOFA-L did.

7 / 7tasks where UniverSat beats DOFA-L, with fewer probe parameters (900K vs 1.2M)

Even a 9K linear probe beats DOFA-L on all 7, and UniverSat comes close to the EnMAP specialist SpectralEarth-L.
